name: Telge Projects Ltd
title: Telge Projects Ltd - 544544 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Asset-light BIM/structural engineering firm with no capacity or utilisation disclosure; growth is acquisition-aided, receivable days jumped 73→108, and 60–70% CAGR guidance is unsupported by a Rs 25 cr order book.

triggers.label: Receivable days 73 → 108
triggers.quote: Receivable days expanded from 73 days to 108 days.

triggers.label: 60–70% CAGR target, no numbers backing
triggers.quote: we are confident to achieve 60% to 70% CAGR growth in the upcoming financial year

triggers.label: Order book Rs 25 cr, pipeline Rs 6 cr
triggers.quote: our current active order book stands at approximately Rs. 25 crores

triggers.label: US hourly rate $25–35 → $45–60 target
triggers.quote: In previous years, we used to stick to rates between $25 to $35 per hour. Now what we are targeting is $45 to $60 per hour even.

we are trying to maintain the same values in the upcoming year. Not trying to go below that.

summary.headline: Telge Projects FY26 revenue rose about 57% to Rs 40.2 crore, with Q4 EBITDA margin of 35% and current order book of about Rs 25 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue from operations of about Rs 40.2 crore (up from Rs 25.6 crore), EBITDA of Rs 9.55 crore at 24% margin and PAT of Rs 5.9 crore at 15% margin. Q4 revenue was Rs 14.4 crore (up 13.7% YoY, about 58% QoQ), with Q4 EBITDA of Rs 5 crore (35% margin) and PAT of Rs 3.3 crore (23% margin). The Edward Farr Architects acquisition closed on 3 March 2026 and contributed only about one month to consolidation. Management guided to 60-70% revenue CAGR and to sustaining Q4-level margins, but gave little visibility beyond the Rs 25 crore order book and a Rs 6 crore RFQ pipeline.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 25.6 crore in FY25, about +57%

financial_highlights.metric: Edward Farr Architects contribution (one month consolidated)
financial_highlights.value: Revenue about Rs 1.5 crore, PAT about Rs 40 lakh

financial_highlights.change: management comment in Q&A, vs about 60% consolidated

segments.name: Structural engineering, BIM and steel detailing (India/US delivery)
segments.commentary: Execution stays in India via the parent company, while US subsidiaries Midwest, Draftco and Edward Farr handle sales and client relations. Management said the subsidiaries' revenue cannot be separated cleanly from the parent.

segments.name: Architectural and interior design (Edward Farr Architects, US)
segments.commentary: Acquired on 3 March 2026 at about 2.5x EBITDA. Calendar 2025 revenue was about Rs 14 crore with PAT margin of 10-12%. Roughly Rs 10 crore of the current order book is attributed to this business.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term revenue CAGR of 60-70%, stated for FY27 and subsequent years.
Management aims to keep FY27 margins at Q4 FY26 levels (EBITDA about 35%, PAT 20-23%) and said it will not go below that.
Target project ticket size raised to Rs 8-10 crore from the previous Rs 2-3 crore.
US billing rates targeted at $45-60 per hour, up from $25-35 previously.
No debt planned; future acquisitions to use other funding. Management said no equity dilution this year.
Acquisition pipeline under evaluation, with Rs 5 crore of IPO proceeds earmarked for acquisitions. MEP services are a targeted capability addition.

qa_highlights.question: What are revenue and margin expectations for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of a 60-70% CAGR in FY27 and subsequent years, and aims to keep EBITDA and PAT at Q4 FY26 levels (EBITDA about 35%, PAT 20-23%) without going below that.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Rs 25 crore order book is from the acquisition, and how much is US-based?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book is a mix of existing business and Edward Farr; Edward Farr architectural work is about Rs 10 crore, and about 80% of the order book is from the US.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 60-70% CAGR inclusive of acquired revenue, and what is the inorganic plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiaries are now treated as organic since operations are shifting to the parent; future inorganic growth will come from new acquisitions, with no specific deal identified yet. MEP services are the targeted capability addition.

qa_highlights.question: Why is receivable days up to 108 from 73?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the major portion of receivables is from a related party; collections were accelerated in April and May, and 60 days DSO is being maintained now. Normal recovery is 30-45 days.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence in 30-35% EBITDA margins versus peers at 20-22%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the US local team enabling higher billing rates ($45-60/hour target versus $25-35), expansion into lower-cost regions such as Nashik and Latur, and AI-led productivity gains.

qa_highlights.question: Is any new debt or equity dilution planned?
qa_highlights.answer: No debt is planned; future acquisitions will use other funding arrangements. Management said no equity dilution is expected this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise sharply, and will it persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Leadership hires (BD heads, HODs, regional heads) and Nashik team expansion were made ahead of growth; FY27 leadership additions are not planned, so cost growth should be lower than in FY26.

capex_capacity: Nashik office became operational during FY26 and supports future scalability; the SDS2 team expanded significantly for steel detailing and connection design, supporting Midwest and Draftco in the US.
Headcount is 200-250 in total, about 25 in the US and the rest in India (Latur, Nashik, Pune); about 70 people added versus last year, with some staff kept on bench ahead of expected growth.
Management said FY27 leadership hiring is not planned; growth in employee cost is expected to come mainly from the execution team.
Capacity expansion in Nashik and Latur is cited as a lever to take on more projects and to lower cost per output.
IPO proceeds: about Rs 7 crore utilised so far; Rs 5 crore re-deployed from office premises purchase to acquisitions per CFO.
demand_pricing: Current active order book of about Rs 25 crore across structural and architectural segments; about 80% from the US, and about Rs 10 crore attributed to Edward Farr architectural business.
RFQ/bidding pipeline of about Rs 6 crore, expected to convert within two weeks to a month.
Order book has been building at about Rs 4-5 crore per month over the last year, per management.
US billing rates targeted at $45-60 per hour versus $25-35 previously; target project ticket size Rs 8-10 crore versus Rs 2-3 crore before.
Customer count 96 in FY26, with about 20 new clients added in Q4, all from the US; 60-70% of revenue from existing clients.
Receivable days rose to 108 from 73; management said 60 days DSO is now being maintained after April-May collections, with the major receivable portion from a related party.
Seasonality is mild: Q2 is typically the slowest quarter, with Q4 usually the strongest.
Management said the Iran-US conflict had no impact on business so far, citing diversified US client base and Australia/Europe exposure.
risks_watch: Receivable days at 108 versus 73 a year ago, with a major share from a related party; the 60-day DSO target must be verified in Q1 FY27 numbers.
Guidance of 60-70% CAGR implies about Rs 60-70 crore revenue next year, far above the Rs 25 crore order book; visibility beyond the current book is limited.
Dependence on US demand (about 80% of order book) and on the Edward Farr architectural business (about Rs 10 crore of order book), with the Iran-US conflict cited as a monitoring point.
Rising employee cost (about 45% of consolidated revenue per analyst, versus about 35%) and the lack of standalone detail on subsidiary performance make margin sustainability hard to verify.
Pricing and margin pressure from AI-led commoditisation of BIM and modelling work, which management did not quantify.
Pending acquisition pipeline with Rs 5 crore of IPO proceeds earmarked; deal size, terms and integration remain unidentified.
key_quotes: In the medium term, we are confident to achieve 60% to 70% CAGR growth in the upcoming financial year, that is FY 2026-27, and relatively the next years as well.
So, the PAT that we have achieved in the Q4 was between 20% to 23%, I guess, and then EBITDA was approximately 35%.
Not trying to go below that.
So, the subsidiaries have zero attrition in that sense.
summary.management_tone: Confident and ambitious on growth (60-70% CAGR, margins held at Q4 levels), but vague on specifics: management declined to quantify Q1 FY27 run rate and gave limited detail on how subsidiary and parent results split. It deflected several questions on the subsidiary-level margins and the receivable spike.

adds.what: Nashik office became operational during FY26 (supports future scalability; no capacity size given)
Capacity expansion in Nashik and Latur cited as lever to take on more projects (no size or timeline given)

growth.why: Management guides 60-70% revenue CAGR for FY27 onward, backed by a Rs 25 crore active order book (about Rs 10 crore from Edward Farr, 80% US), a Rs 6 crore RFQ pipeline, and higher billing rates and ticket sizes, but no specific capacity additions with numbers or timing are given.
